title: Zariski descent and cover independence of synchronized ordinary resolution towers
statement:
Fix a totally ordered set $L$. Over $\mathbf Q$, let $\mathcal C$ be the reduced finite-type schemes admitting a closed embedding into a smooth separated finite-type scheme, including finite disjoint unions of such inputs [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Suppose $A$ assigns to every $X\in\mathcal C$ a finite ordinary blowup tower $A(X)$, with distinct labels in increasing order in $L$, coherent ideal centers whose zero schemes are nonempty nowhere dense and regular, and regular final scheme [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule, def-nagata-global-blowup, pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Nowhere dense means empty interior of the underlying closed set. Suppose $A(\varnothing)$ is trivial. For every open immersion $j:X'\to X$ in $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-open-immersion], assume $A(X')$ is canonically the contraction of $j^*A(X)$, preserving labels and extended ideals [def-nagata-extended-ideal]; precisely the unit-ideal stages are deleted. Comparisons are the canonical ordinary blowup comparisons.

Then $A$ extends, uniquely up to canonical isomorphisms preserving labels and center ideals, to an assignment $R$ of such regular ordinary resolution towers on every reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme $S$, without a separatedness assumption. For every finite affine open cover $\{U_a\}$ of $S$, put $U=\coprod_a U_a$. The tower $R(S)$ has exactly the label list of $A(U)$, and its cartesian pullback to $U$ is $A(U)$ without any contraction [def-pc-fibre-product]. More precisely, on an affine open $W\subset U_a\cap U_b$ the two restrictions of $A(U)$ agree as towers with centers after restoring the unit-ideal identity stages at the missing labels of $A(W)$. These agreements hold also on triple overlaps. At each label the ideals on the corresponding lifted open cover descend to one coherent ideal on the current level of $S$, and the next level is its ordinary blowup. Every resulting center is nonempty, nowhere dense and regular, the final scheme is regular, and all levels remain of finite type over $\mathbf Q$.

For two finite affine covers, the towers obtained using them are canonically identified, preserving their labels and all level ideals, by the comparison with their combined covering family; neither original covering family loses a label of the combined tower. These identifications are transitive for three covers. The restriction of $R$ to $\mathcal C$ is canonically $A$, and $R(\varnothing)$ is trivial. No intersection of affine opens is assumed affine.

proof.text: Obtain padded affine overlap compatibility from [lem-trf-ordinary-resolution-padded-overlaps]. Apply [lem-trf-affine-resolution-descent-existence] separately to every input and choose a family R of the resulting regular affine descents. This is choice inside the proof of an existential theorem, not a definition or a choice of unconstructed data for a public object.

Prove uniqueness of cartesian ordinary tower maps over any fixed base map directly by induction on levels. At zero cancel the initial isomorphism in the commuting pullback square. At a successor the source center becomes invertible after its blowup by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center]; its blowup isomorphism is flat. The center equality identifies this with the target center pulled back along the common lower map. Apply uniqueness of lifts in [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] to identify the two successor maps, then cancel the target blowup isomorphism. Proof irrelevance identifies all remaining structure fields. No regularity or cover assumption is needed.

Apply [lem-trf-affine-resolution-descent-comparison] to each chosen R(S). Its first part gives existence of the full map on every cover with DescendsIdeals; the preceding uniqueness promotes this to the required unique map. Its second part gives comparison existence with every affine descent, again promoted to Unique. By [lem-trf-embedded-resolution-affine-descent], A(S) on an embeddable input is such an affine descent, giving the embedded-input comparison.

For empty S, unpack the affine-descent witness T to R(S). The morphism T to S makes T empty, so A.empty gives its length zero. The full comparison identifies this length with that of R(S). For two covers, their full comparisons to R(S) identify each label range with the label range of R(S), since finite-index casts are bijective and the maps preserve labels. Transitivity of equality gives the required label-range equality.

For three arbitrary labeled cartesian maps over the identity, identify their equal lengths and compare the levelwise composite with the direct map. Both have the same zero map by the commuting base squares. Compose their adjacent-arrow equalities using associativity, and compose their center equalities using functoriality of extended ideals. The same blowup-lift induction already used for uniqueness now identifies these level maps. This proves the required IsComposite equation without a further descent or cocycle assumption.

lean.statement: theorem exists_synchronized_resolution_zariski_descent (L : Type w) [LinearOrder L] (A : OrdinaryZariskiResolutionRule.{u, w} L) : ∃ R : ∀ S : RationalResolutionInput.{u}, LabeledOrdinaryTower L S.scheme, (∀ S, (R S).IsResolution) ∧ (∀ S, IsEmpty S.scheme → (R S).tower.length = 0) ∧ (∀ (S : RationalResolutionInput.{u}) (hS : S.IsEmbeddable), Nonempty (Unique (LabeledOrdinaryCartesianMap (𝟙 S.scheme) (R S) (A.tower S hS)))) ∧ (∀ S, A.IsSynchronizedDescent S (R S)) ∧ A.HasPaddedOverlaps ∧ (∀ (S T V : RationalResolutionInput.{u}) (q : T.scheme ⟶ S.scheme) (r : V.scheme ⟶ S.scheme), ResolutionAffineCover S T q → ResolutionAffineCover S V r → ∃ (hT : T.IsEmbeddable) (hV : V.IsEmbeddable), Set.range (A.tower T hT).label = Set.range (A.tower V hV).label) ∧ (∀ (S : RationalResolutionInput.{u}) (B : LabeledOrdinaryTower L S.scheme), A.IsAffineDescent S B → Nonempty (Unique (LabeledOrdinaryCartesianMap (𝟙 S.scheme) (R S) B))) ∧ (∀ (S : RationalResolutionInput.{u}) (B C D : LabeledOrdinaryTower L S.scheme), A.IsAffineDescent S B → A.IsAffineDescent S C → A.IsAffineDescent S D → ∀ (bc : LabeledOrdinaryCartesianMap (𝟙 S.scheme) B C) (cd : LabeledOrdinaryCartesianMap (𝟙 S.scheme) C D) (bd : LabeledOrdinaryCartesianMap (𝟙 S.scheme) B D), bc.IsComposite cd bd)
